guidelines.detail: same as LRN-057 (The description explicitly states a sending action, but the reference task for that action has no counterpart in the generated model. This guideline addresses that omission and is essentially covered by learned guideline LRN-057. The separate missing exclusive gateway is addressed by documented guideline GW-02.)

same as LRN-081 (The generated labels omit the participant named in the description, while the reference labels retain that attribution. This is supported by the label pairs and description records; the separate missing-task record does not establish a label difference.)

same as LRN-050 (The description identifies sending as an activity. The missing task and generated start event indicate that this activity was modeled using the wrong BPMN element. LRN-050 already says to use a task for performed work and an event for an occurrence.)

same as LRN-050 (The description explicitly states the sending activity, and the reference includes it while the generated model has no counterpart. LRN-050 already covers modeling a described communication activity itself as the appropriate message-flow endpoint, using a task for performed work.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant must send a report or other information to a recipient: model the reporting action itself as a send task when sending the information is the work being performed, rather than as a generic service task
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states that a participant sends information or an item to another participant before the recipient performs a subsequent action.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description assigns an action to a participant or states the direction of an interaction: Preserve who performs or receives the action and its direction in the BPMN element label; do not relabel receipt as sending or otherwise change the stated action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns an activity to a participant and that responsibility helps distinguish who performs it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one participant’s described activity or occurrence communicates information or an item to another participant: Model the described activity or occurrence itself as the appropriate message-flow endpoint: use a task for performed work and an event for an occurrence. Do not add a separate send task merely to carry the same communication.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant sends information or an item to another participant as an activity
